For a finite MDP with bounded rewards, a policy assigns a probability distribution on $A(s)$ to each finite observed history ending in state $s$, with each action probability a measurable function of the history; deterministic policies are included. For states $x,y$, start at $S_0=x$ and define $\tau_y=\inf\{t\ge0:S_t=y\}$, with $\tau_y=+\infty$ if $y$ is never hit. This is an extended nonnegative measurable random variable because $\{\tau_y\le n\}=\bigcup_{t=0}^n\{S_t=y\}$. Take the expectation and the infimum over policies in $[0,+\infty]$. The MDP is communicating if $\inf_\pi\mathbb E_x^\pi[\tau_y]<\infty$ for every ordered pair $(x,y)$. Its raw diameter is $D_0=\sup_{x,y}\inf_\pi\mathbb E_x^\pi[\tau_y]$ in $[0,+\infty]$, and its normalized diameter is $D=\max\{1,D_0\}$ in the extended order. Since $S$ is finite, $D_0$ is finite for every communicating MDP. Thus a one-state MDP has $D_0=0$ and $D=1$.
